title: Parish and Ledger
premise: Quentin Underhill, the meticulous archivist of St. Aldhelm's Cathedral, receives a confession letter postmarked the day after the funeral of Canon Edgar Mowbray — a letter claiming the canon's death was murder and naming Quentin's own predecessor as an accomplice. As they dig through twelve years of carefully alphabetized records, Quentin discovers the crypt's lock was changed the night of the funeral, and that the town's most powerful families have been paying the cathedral to keep certain ledgers sealed. The trail leads to a decades-old cover-up of a drowned choirboy whose death funded the cathedral's restoration, and Quentin must decide whether justice belongs in a courtroom or in the open air. In the end, Quentin unlocks the crypt before the bishop can destroy the ledgers, exposing the conspiracy at the memorial service — but chooses to burn one page: the confession naming their own father among the payers.
about_author: Noor Vane is the pen name of a former parish secretary who spent nine years cataloguing diocesan archives in northern England before turning to fiction. They write mysteries about paper trails, small towns, and the people who keep both.

chapters.title: The Alphabet of Grief
chapters.summary: Quentin Underhill files condolence cards from Canon Mowbray's funeral, establishing their ordered world and quiet loneliness. A letter arrives, postmarked the day after the burial, unsigned: 'He did not die in his sleep. Check the 1998 ledger.' POV: Quentin. Emotional beat: unease cracking open a settled life.

chapters.title: Twelve Years of Dust
chapters.summary: Quentin searches the archive for the 1998 ledger and finds its shelf slot empty, though the catalogue card remains. The head verger, Mrs. Tallow, watches them too closely. POV: Quentin. Emotional beat: first vertigo of realizing the archive itself has been edited.

chapters.title: What the Verger Saw
chapters.summary: Quentin interviews Mrs. Tallow under pretense of funeral paperwork; she reveals someone entered the archive the night after the funeral using a key only three people hold. POV: Quentin. Emotional beat: the closed circle tightens — suspicion becomes personal.

chapters.title: The Bishop's Courtesy
chapters.summary: Bishop Anselm Crane summons Quentin, warmly warns them against 'morbid speculation,' and offers a promotion that would move them away from the archive. POV: Quentin. Emotional beat: flattery as threat; power shows its smiling face.

chapters.title: A Drowned Boy's Name
chapters.summary: In the newspaper morgue, Quentin finds a 1998 clipping: choirboy Samuel Peake drowned in the flooded quarry; ruled accidental. The restoration campaign began weeks later, suspiciously well-funded. POV: Quentin. Emotional beat: grief for a stranger hardens into purpose.

chapters.title: Intercession
chapters.summary: Quentin visits Samuel's mother, Ruth Peake, who has petitioned the diocese for answers for twenty-five years and been stonewalled each time — always by the same solicitor's firm. POV: Quentin. Emotional beat: inheritance of another kind — a mother's unfinished case passed on.

chapters.title: The Solicitor's Ledger
chapters.summary: Breaking into the law firm's dead storage, Quentin finds donation ledgers showing the town's leading families paid the cathedral hush sums after 1998 — including the Underhill name. POV: Quentin. Emotional beat: betrayal; the hunt turns inward.

chapters.title: My Father's Handwriting
chapters.summary: Quentin confronts their estranged father, Gerald, a retired bank manager, who admits signing a payment but claims he was protecting the cathedral, not covering a crime. He begs Quentin to stop. POV: Quentin. Emotional beat: filial loyalty versus truth; the theme of inheritance sharpens.

chapters.title: Second Postmark
chapters.summary: A second anonymous letter arrives, quoting Mowbray's exact words from his deathbed — proof the writer was present when he died. Quentin realizes the confessor is either the killer or a witness. POV: Quentin. Emotional beat: fear arrives; the game is being played with them.

chapters.title: The Crypt Key
chapters.summary: Quentin discovers the crypt lock was replaced the night after the funeral and that Mowbray had requested access to it two days before he died. Below lies what he wanted found. POV: Quentin. Emotional beat: the locked room becomes the story's beating heart.

chapters.title: Mrs. Tallow's Silence
chapters.summary: Quentin presses Mrs. Tallow; she breaks down, admitting she saw the bishop's chaplain carrying a box from the crypt at midnight, and has been paid to forget it since 1998. POV: Quentin. Emotional beat: complicity of ordinary people; pity entangled with anger.

chapters.title: Chaplain Down
chapters.summary: Before Quentin can reach him, the chaplain is found dead on the quarry path — officially another accident. Police close ranks fast; the investigating sergeant is the solicitor's brother-in-law. POV: Quentin. Emotional beat: horror and isolation; the law itself is compromised.

chapters.title: Justice Outside the Law
chapters.summary: Ruth Peake proposes they bypass police entirely: gather evidence and read it aloud publicly. Quentin resists, then agrees, understanding the courts were bought long ago. POV: alternating Quentin/Ruth. Emotional beat: alliance forged; the theme of extralegal justice made explicit.

chapters.title: The Restoration File
chapters.summary: Quentin reconstructs the money trail: Samuel's death triggered an insurance payout funneled through the families into the restoration fund — the cathedral literally rebuilt on a boy's grave. POV: Quentin. Emotional beat: cold clarity; corruption given architecture.

chapters.title: Threats in the Stacks
chapters.summary: The archive is ransacked overnight; the 1998 catalogue cards are gone. Quentin survives a staged fall from the gallery stairs and understands they are now disposable. POV: Quentin. Emotional beat: terror transmuted into defiance.

chapters.title: Gerald's Confession
chapters.summary: Gerald Underhill, shaken by the chaplain's death, gives Quentin his copy of the ledger and admits the families met the night Samuel died — and that Mowbray was there too, taking his share. POV: Gerald, framed within Quentin's visit. Emotional beat: a father's shame; inheritance as burden.

chapters.title: Who Wrote the Letters
chapters.summary: Quentin identifies the handwriting: the letters match Mowbray's own hand — dictated before death to someone he trusted, mailed on a timer by the only person with archive keys besides Quentin. All signs point to Mrs. Tallow. POV: Quentin. Emotional beat: devastating realization that an ally orchestrated everything.

chapters.title: Tallow's Bargain
chapters.summary: Confronted, Mrs. Tallow confesses she was Samuel's aunt; Mowbray, dying, gave her the letters as penance. She admits she also warned the bishop, hoping to force him to confess rather than be exposed. POV: Mrs. Tallow. Emotional beat: grief weaponized; vengeance and justice blur.

chapters.title: Night Before the Memorial
chapters.summary: The bishop announces a memorial service where the new restoration wing will be dedicated. Quentin learns the remaining ledgers will be burned in the crypt furnace afterward. One night to act. POV: Quentin. Emotional beat: ticking clock; resolve crystallizes.

chapters.title: The Locked Crypt
chapters.summary: Quentin picks the new lock with the old key's impression, finds the original 1998 ledger hidden in Mowbray's coffin niche, and narrowly escapes as the chaplain's replacement comes to feed the furnace. POV: Quentin. Emotional beat: climax of nerve; the past physically recovered from the grave.

chapters.title: Read Aloud
chapters.summary: At the memorial, before the whole town, Quentin and Ruth read the ledger entries and Mowbray's confession from the pulpit. The bishop collapses mid-denial; the sergeant tries to arrest them, but too many families are named for anyone to move. POV: Quentin. Emotional beat: catharsis; justice spoken into the open air.

chapters.title: One Page Burned
chapters.summary: Weeks later, investigations begin and Ruth finally buries her son properly. Quentin burns the single ledger page bearing their father's signature, keeps the rest, and reopens the crypt to the public — a museum of what the town did. POV: Quentin. Emotional beat: bittersweet resolution; mercy chosen alongside justice.
